description: P4.6 (TASKS.md): track every version/commit/digest pin this repo maintains by
hand. See docs/renovate.md for the full inventory of what is managed here,
what is deliberately excluded, and why.
STATUS (2026-07-14): Renovate is INSTALLED on this repository and this config
is live. It validates clean against the official tool:
npx --package renovate -- renovate-config-validator renovate.json
Run that before pushing any change to this file -- an invalid config makes
Renovate skip the repo silently rather than fail loudly.
BUT NOTE (2026-07-18): the validator only checks SHAPE, not whether a manager
matches anything. Both bugs fixed today were validator-clean and silent:
1. managerFilePatterns entries are GLOB patterns unless slash-delimited.
`^Makefile$` is a valid glob that matches no file; `/^Makefile$/` is the
regex that works. (This field replaced fileMatch, which was ALWAYS regex --
so the semantics changed under an unchanged-looking value.) All 18 custom
managers were silently extracting zero deps.
2. The kernel custom datasource returned a bare object instead of a one-element
array -- see its own description below.
The only reliable check is a real extraction run, which needs no GitHub token:
npx --package renovate@latest -- renovate --platform=local --dry-run=full
Expect a `regex` entry in the 'Dependency extraction complete' stats with
fileCount 23 / depCount 24 (2026-08-17, 22 customManagers). RE-DERIVE BOTH
whenever a manager is added or a managerFilePatterns entry changes -- neither
number is the manager count, and this pair had already gone stale silently:
18/19 was measured at commit e66b46b when there were 18 managers, and nothing
updated it when 2ae2d5f gave the 6.18 manager a second defconfig and added the
RT manager. How they are derived, so the next person can recompute instead of
guessing: fileCount is one per (manager, matched file) PAIR, not per distinct
file -- scripts/fetch-sdcard-payload.sh is counted three times because three
managers match it. depCount is one per regex MATCH, which is why it runs one
ahead of fileCount here: configs/mister_de10nano_defconfig carries
BR2_LINUX_KERNEL_CUSTOM_VERSION_VALUE="..." twice -- line 146, the real
setting, and line 41 inside a header comment, which a regex manager has no
reason to skip. That model was validated by replaying it over the tree at
e66b46b, where it reproduces the recorded 18/19 exactly.
If `regex` is absent entirely, the custom managers are dead again. Grep the
LOG_LEVEL=debug output for `no-result` to catch bug-2-style
datasource failures, which do NOT show up in the extraction stats at all.
AND IT HAD GONE STALE AGAIN, exactly as this note predicts of itself: the
recorded pair was 22/23 until 2026-08-17, when a real extraction measured
23/24 -- the dualsensectl manager landed after the 22/23 measurement and
nothing re-derived the numbers. Measured on BOTH master and the 7.2 branch
that refreshed this line, which is the only way to tell 'the tree grew a
manager' from 'my change moved the count': the 7.2 RT-pin rewrite is
count-NEUTRAL (same managers, same file patterns, one match each) and the
whole delta predates it. Note the `no-result` grep above now has nine
false positives -- the literal string appears inside the descriptions that
warn about it, this one included. Read the hits, do not just count them.
automerge is OFF everywhere, deliberately: every pin here is a supply-chain
trust decision (kernel, Buildroot, out-of-tree driver commits, firmware), and
several need a companion hash refreshed by .github/workflows/renovate-hash-sync.yml
before the PR is even buildable. A human reviews each one.

kernelLongterm618.description: kernel.org's machine-readable releases.json, filtered down to the current 6.18.y longterm point release. Deliberately constrained by moniker+prefix here (not just by allowedVersions below) so a schema hiccup upstream can't silently hand back mainline/other-branch versions. NOTE the outer [ ] around the $map: releases.json lists only the LATEST release per branch, so this filter always matches exactly one entry, and JSONata collapses a single-element sequence into a bare object. Renovate's custom datasource requires `releases` to be an ARRAY -- without the explicit array constructor it receives an object, fails schema validation, and reports `no-result` (a silent no-op, not an error). Do not remove the brackets.

kernelStable72.description: kernel.org's releases.json filtered to the 7.2 LINE -- what the RT/beta kernel variant tracks (configs/mister_rt.fragment, docs/rt-beta-kernel.md). RENAMED AND REWRITTEN 2026-08-17, when 7.2 released and the pin crossed the -rc boundary; it was `kernelMainline` and filtered on moniker=mainline, which was right while 7.2 was in -rc and became actively WRONG the moment it shipped: mainline moves on to 7.3-rc1 within about two weeks of a release, so the old filter would have proposed dragging the beta variant off the line it had just reached and back into permanent -rc churn. docs/rt-beta-kernel.md picks 7.2 because PREEMPT_RT for 32-bit ARM landed in 7.1, and 7.2 final was always the intended DESTINATION of this pin, not a waypoint. Moving to 7.3+ is now a deliberate human edit of this datasource, mirroring how kernelLongterm618 hardcodes 6.18. WHY THE FILTER IS MONIKER-AGNOSTIC, which is the one thing to understand before touching it: the 7.2 line changes moniker underneath us. TODAY 7.2 is the `mainline` entry and no 7.2.y stable release exists yet (stable is still 7.1.8), so a moniker=stable filter would match NOTHING and report `no-result` -- a silent no-op, exactly the bug class this file's header warns about. Once 7.2.1 ships, 7.2.y becomes the `stable` entry and mainline becomes 7.3-rcN. Matching on the VERSION rather than the moniker is what spans that handover without a flag day. The `= "7.2"` clause is the two-component release itself; the `$substring(...,0,4) = "7.2."` clause is every later 7.2.y point release. The trailing dot is load-bearing (it is what stops 7.21 matching) and $substring is used rather than $contains so a hypothetical 17.2.x could never match either. TRIPWIRE: when the 7.2 line goes EOL and drops out of releases.json, this filter matches nothing and the pin SILENTLY stops being managed -- no PR, no error. That is the moment to make the deliberate decision about which line the variant tracks next, and the only way to notice it is the dependency dashboard going quiet, so check it if this pin has been still for a long time. The outer [ ] is required for the same reason documented above -- this filter matches exactly one entry, and JSONata would collapse a single-element sequence into a bare object, which Renovate rejects as `no-result` silently.

customManagers.description: Bump the pinned Buildroot release (BUILDROOT_VERSION) in the wrapper Makefile. Deliberately does NOT try to also update the companion BUILDROOT_SHA256 on the next line -- that hash is only legitimate when transcribed from Buildroot's own GPG-signed release manifest (the Makefile's own header comment forbids a locally-computed sha256sum, since that would be circular and would bless a tampered/truncated tarball). A human runs `make buildroot-showsig BUILDROOT_VERSION=<new>` and pastes the signed hash in by hand -- see docs/renovate.md. Until then this PR is RED (buildroot-verify fails closed), which is the intended, safe failure mode.

Bump the pinned 6.18.y kernel (BR2_LINUX_KERNEL_CUSTOM_VERSION_VALUE) EVERYWHERE it appears, constrained to the current longterm line by the custom datasource above. BOTH defconfigs are listed on purpose: configs/mister_kernel_defconfig deliberately copies the main defconfig's kernel/toolchain stanza (see its header and scripts/check-kernel-defconfig-sync.sh), so a manager covering only the main one bumps half the repo and leaves the copy behind -- which is exactly what happened on the 6.18.38 -> 6.18.39 bump and is caught, loudly, by the lockstep check. Because both files carry the same depName, Renovate emits ONE PR touching both. configs/mister_rt.fragment carries the same SYMBOL but is deliberately NOT matched here: it pins the mainline -rc line and has its own manager below. The companion tarball hash (board/mister/de10nano/patches/linux/linux.hash) is NOT updated here -- it comes from kernel.org's own signed sha256sums.asc; see .github/workflows/renovate-hash-sync.yml. CI (build.yml, pull_request-triggered) then proves the carried Linux patches still apply against the bumped source -- see docs/renovate.md and PLAN.md §13.

Bump the RT/beta kernel pin (BR2_LINUX_KERNEL_CUSTOM_VERSION_VALUE in configs/mister_rt.fragment), which tracks the 7.2 line rather than 6.18.y -- see docs/rt-beta-kernel.md and ADR 0021. Kept as a SEPARATE manager from the 6.18 one above, with its own datasource and its own depName, because the two must never be able to propose each other's version: the fragment carries the identical Kconfig symbol, so a single shared manager would hand one datasource the other's currentValue. UPDATED 2026-08-17, when 7.2 released and this pin crossed the -rc boundary (7.2-rc7 -> 7.2); the depName went `kernel-mainline-rt` -> `kernel-rt-7.2` because the old one now describes a line this pin deliberately no longer follows. Renaming a depName orphans any open branch under the old name and starts a fresh dependency-dashboard entry -- that was accepted as a one-off cost, not overlooked. THE matchString MUST ACCEPT THREE FORMS and the reason is a silent-failure trap: `7.2-rc7` (history, and the shape it would return to if a human ever repoints this at an -rc), `7.2` (a two-component release -- what kernel.org actually publishes for a .0), and `7.2.1` (every later point release on this line). The three-component alternative is not hypothetical padding: the moment 7.2.1 lands and Renovate writes it here, a matchString that only accepted two components would stop matching its own output, extract zero deps, and silently leave the pin unmanaged forever -- validator-clean and invisible, exactly the failure mode this file's header describes. THE COMPANION HASH IS NOW AUTO-REFRESHED, which reverses what this description said until 2026-08-17: linux-7.2.tar.xz is an ordinary release tarball covered by kernel.org's PGP-signed sha256sums.asc, so scripts/hash-sync-kernel.sh handles this pin as its `rt` case and a routine 7.2.y bump PR can go green on its own. That script REFUSES any value containing `-rc` (kernel.org signs no manifest for a cgit snapshot, so such a hash can only be hand-written TOFU) and leaves the line untouched, so the build fails closed at the kernel download rather than blessing an unexamined snapshot -- see linux.hash's own header and docs/ci.md#renovate-hash-sync-not-automated. allowedVersions below keeps -rc out of this manager's reach in the first place; the script's refusal is the second line of defense for a hand edit.
RTL8812AU driver commit pin (morrownr/8812au-20210820, main branch). Hash: package/rtl8812au/rtl8812au.hash, refreshed by renovate-hash-sync.yml.
RTL8814AU driver commit pin (morrownr/8814au, main branch). Hash: package/rtl8814au-morrownr/rtl8814au-morrownr.hash, refreshed by renovate-hash-sync.yml.
RTL8821AU driver commit pin (morrownr/8821au-20210708, main branch). Hash: package/rtl8821au-morrownr/rtl8821au-morrownr.hash, refreshed by renovate-hash-sync.yml.
RTL8821CU driver commit pin (morrownr/8821cu-20210916, main branch). Hash: package/rtl8821cu-morrownr/rtl8821cu-morrownr.hash, refreshed by renovate-hash-sync.yml.
RTL8188FU driver commit pin (kelebek333/rtl8188fu, master branch). Hash: package/rtl8188fu/rtl8188fu.hash, refreshed by renovate-hash-sync.yml.

RTL8188EU driver commit pin (aircrack-ng/rtl8188eus). NOTE: this repo's default branch is literally named 'v5.3.9' (verified via git ls-remote --symref at authoring time, not assumed) -- update currentValueTemplate if aircrack-ng ever renames it, or this manager will quietly stop finding new commits. Hash: package/rtl8188eu-aircrack-ng/rtl8188eu-aircrack-ng.hash, refreshed by renovate-hash-sync.yml.
RTL88X2BU driver commit pin (morrownr/88x2bu-20210702, main branch). Hash: package/rtl88x2bu/rtl88x2bu.hash, refreshed by renovate-hash-sync.yml.

RTL8852CU driver commit pin (morrownr/rtl8852cu-20251113, main branch). `main` is the right ref to track and was checked, not assumed: `git ls-remote https://github.com/morrownr/rtl8852cu-20251113` resolves HEAD and refs/heads/main to the same commit (1530c38e at pin time). Hash: package/rtl8852cu-morrownr/rtl8852cu-morrownr.hash, refreshed by renovate-hash-sync.yml's GENERIC loop -- this package needs no bespoke step: its site is a plain $(call github,morrownr,rtl8852cu-20251113,$(VERSION)) and Buildroot caches the tarball as dl/rtl8852cu-morrownr/rtl8852cu-morrownr-<sha>.tar.gz, i.e. exactly the <package-dir>-<VERSION>.tar.gz shape scripts/hash-sync-github-packages.sh assumes. UNLIKE every other Realtek fork pin in this block, this one is for a driver the image ACTUALLY SHIPS (ADR 0016's v10.2 update: rtw89 carries the 8852C chip HAL but no rtw8852cu.c USB bus file, and its only symbol RTW89_8852CE depends on PCI, which this board has not got -- so mainline cannot drive the chip at all). The others are kept sourced-but-deselected as a one-line revert. THREE places move together for this pin, and two of them fail SILENTLY if forgotten: this manager, `rtl8852cu-morrownr` in renovate-hash-sync.yml's HASH_SYNC_PACKAGES (absent = the hash is never refreshed and the build fails on a mismatch that reads like a tampered upstream), and this .mk in that same workflow's `paths:` trigger (absent = the workflow never fires at all -- no skipped job, no red X, nothing).
xone (Xbox GIP) driver commit pin (dlundqvist/xone, master branch). Hash: package/xone/xone.hash, refreshed by renovate-hash-sync.yml.
MidiLink_MiSTer commit pin (MiSTer-devel/MidiLink_MiSTer, master branch). Hash: package/midilink/midilink.hash, refreshed by renovate-hash-sync.yml.

munt MT-32 emulator tag pin. Non-standard tag format (munt_MAJOR_MINOR_PATCH) needs a regex versioning scheme so Renovate orders releases correctly instead of treating the whole string as an opaque blob. Hash: package/munt/munt.hash, refreshed by renovate-hash-sync.yml.

dualsensectl tag pin (nowrep/dualsensectl) -- the DualSense operator CLI, a userspace tool, NOT a substitute for the DualSense kernel patches (see package/dualsensectl/dualsensectl.mk and docs/dualsense-tooling.md). Upstream tags plain vMAJOR.MINOR releases, so `loose` needs no bespoke scheme here, unlike munt above. The leading "v" is deliberately INSIDE the captured currentValue rather than being reconstructed in the .mk's SITE line: scripts/hash-sync-github-packages.sh takes the literal RHS of the first *_VERSION line and uses it both as the archive ref and as the <pkgdir>-<version>.tar.gz filename it writes into the .hash, so the two must agree character for character. Renovate rewrites the captured group in place and therefore preserves the prefix. Hash: package/dualsensectl/dualsensectl.hash, refreshed by renovate-hash-sync.yml's generic loop (standard $(call github,...) archive tarball).

BCM20702 Bluetooth firmware COMMIT pin (winterheart/broadcom-bt-firmware, master branch). Was a github-tags/loose TAG pin until 2026-07-19; changed for two independent reasons. (1) Upstream stopped tagging: the newest tag v12.0.1.1105_p4 is from 2022-10-10, while master is still active (three firmware commits on 2026-07-08), so a tag pin could no longer see real updates. (2) The tag scheme actively misled the ordering: the trailing _pN is a patch level ON TOP of the base version, so v12.0.1.1105_p4 is NEWER than v12.0.1.1105 -- but under `loose` the bare tag sorts higher, and Renovate kept proposing v12.0.1.1105 (2020-05-02) as an upgrade, i.e. a 2.5-year DOWNGRADE. A commit pin removes the ordering question entirely instead of trying to teach `loose` a bespoke scheme, and matches how the 10 other untagged upstreams here are pinned (the driver commit-SHA pins -- 9 of them when this was written on 2026-07-19, 10 since rtl8852cu-morrownr joined them in v10.2). Safe because the package installs exactly ONE file and the .mk's inline sha256sum of that .hcd fails the build CLOSED if it ever changes -- the switch itself was a verified no-op (the .hcd is byte-identical at the old tag and at master). Hash: package/bcm20702-firmware/bcm20702-firmware.hash, refreshed by renovate-hash-sync.yml's generic loop.

libchdr commit pin (rtissera/libchdr, master branch) -- the CHD read library for the Main_MiSTer shared-lib refactor; pinned to a branch-head commit, not the stale v0.3.0 tag (see libchdr.mk's header for why). Hash: package/libchdr/libchdr.hash, refreshed by renovate-hash-sync.yml's generic loop (standard $(call github,...) tarball).

7-Zip LZMA SDK tag pin (ip7z/7zip) for the Main_MiSTer shared-lib refactor. Only the LZMA_SDK_VERSION line needs managing -- LZMA_SDK_SOURCE derives from it via $(subst) in the .mk. Hash: package/lzma-sdk/lzma-sdk.hash, refreshed by renovate-hash-sync.yml's BESPOKE ip7z/7zip step (scripts/hash-sync-ip7z-src.sh -- release-asset URL with a dots-stripped filename, does not fit the generic $(call github,...) loop). That step is table-driven over BOTH packages that pin this asset: this one and package/7zip (ADR 0023).

7-Zip application tag pin (ip7z/7zip) for package/7zip -- the `7zz` archiver AND the statically-linked /media/fat/linux/7za that replaces the p7zip 16.02 binary the Downloader used to fetch off the internet (ADR 0023). SAME depName as the lzma-sdk manager above ON PURPOSE: both pin the identical release asset, so Renovate raises ONE PR bumping both .mk files and they cannot silently drift apart. Only the 7ZIP_VERSION line needs managing -- 7ZIP_SOURCE derives from it via $(subst) in the .mk. Hash: package/7zip/7zip.hash, refreshed by the same BESPOKE step in renovate-hash-sync.yml (scripts/hash-sync-ip7z-src.sh, table-driven over both packages).

azcopy release pin (Azure/azure-storage-azcopy) -- Microsoft's Azure Storage CLI, carried for off-device backup of the exFAT data partition. Upstream tags are v-prefixed (v10.32.7) but AZCOPY_VERSION holds the BARE version and azcopy.mk reconstructs the "v" in its SITE line -- the opposite of the dualsensectl/munt convention here, and deliberate; the comment above AZCOPY_VERSION says why. extractVersionTemplate strips the tag's "v" so Renovate compares and writes bare versions. THE HASH IS NOT AUTO-REFRESHED AND CANNOT BE. azcopy is a golang-package, so the file Buildroot hashes is the post-`go mod vendor` -go2 tarball, not the GitHub archive; scripts/hash-sync-github-packages.sh's `curl | sha256sum` method would write a plausible-looking WRONG value, so azcopy is deliberately ABSENT from HASH_SYNC_PACKAGES in renovate-hash-sync.yml -- do not add it there. Every bump PR therefore FAILS CLOSED on the stale hash (BR2_DOWNLOAD_FORCE_CHECK_HASHES=y) until a human runs the regeneration recipe in package/azcopy/azcopy.hash: the same deliberate posture as the RT kernel pin. A bump must also re-verify that both ARMv7 patches still apply -- 0002 patches a VENDORED file, so a github.com/wastore/keyctl bump is meant to break it loudly. See docs/azcopy.md.

Update_All_MiSTer launcher pinned into the sdcard payload (theypsilon/Update_All_MiSTer, master branch). Tracks the branch HEAD and bumps the 40-char commit; the SHA-256/size companions (PINNED_UPDATE_ALL_SHA256/SIZE in the same file) are refreshed by renovate-hash-sync.yml.

wifi.sh pinned into the sdcard payload (MiSTer-devel/Scripts_MiSTer other_authors/wifi.sh, master branch). Tracks the branch HEAD and bumps the 40-char commit; the SHA-256/size companions (PINNED_WIFI_SH_SHA256/SIZE in the same file) are refreshed by renovate-hash-sync.yml.

_Console cores snapshot commit for the opt-in sdcard-full.img (MiSTer-devel/Distribution_MiSTer, main branch). Commit-only pin -- individual cores are fetched by content, not hash-verified (see scripts/fetch-sdcard-payload.sh), so there is no companion hash to sync.

packageRules.description: Constrain the Buildroot pin to the 2026.05.x line -- do not let Renovate jump to a new Buildroot major/minor; P1.1's whole toolchain/config pin assumes 2026.05. (2026.05 is NOT an LTS; 2025.02 was the last LTS and 2027.02 is expected to be the next -- see docs. This is the interim non-LTS line until 2027.02 ships.)

Constrain the kernel pin to the 6.18.y longterm line (defense in depth -- the custom datasource above already filters to moniker=longterm and 6.18.*). A kernel MINOR bump is out of scope for routine automation and must not be silently allowed here.

RT/beta kernel pin (configs/mister_rt.fragment), tracking the 7.2 line. TIGHTENED 2026-08-17 from /^7\./ to the 7.2 line specifically, at the same time the datasource stopped filtering on moniker=mainline: the two together are what keep this pin ON 7.2 now that it has arrived there. /^7\./ was correct while 7.2 was in -rc (it fenced off a MAJOR jump, the only jump that mattered then) but it would have waved 7.3-rc1 straight through about two weeks after 7.2 shipped. Defense in depth, mirroring the 6.18 rule above: the datasource already scopes to 7.2, and this is the second, independent statement of the same intent -- moving the beta variant to a new upstream LINE is a deliberate decision, not routine automation, and it takes edits in both places. The pattern admits 7.2 and 7.2.N and nothing else; note it also excludes every -rc, so Renovate cannot walk this pin back across the boundary it just crossed. Labeled distinctly from kernel-pin so a reviewer is never in doubt about WHICH kernel a PR moves -- the two carry the identical Kconfig symbol and otherwise look alike in a diff. needs-manual-hash was DROPPED on 2026-08-17 and its absence is a claim, not an oversight: a 7.2.y tarball is covered by kernel.org's signed manifest, so scripts/hash-sync-kernel.sh's `rt` case refreshes linux.hash on the PR and it can go green unattended. The label would have to come back if this pin were ever hand-pointed at an -rc again, which allowedVersions above now prevents Renovate from doing on its own. needs-manual-version-check STAYS, with a sharper meaning than the `loose`-ordering worry it was originally carried for (that worry is largely moot once -rc is out of range): every version bump re-opens the RT variant's hardware-boot claim, which is per-version and cannot be inherited from the previous pin -- see docs/rt-beta-kernel.md §6.
Driver/firmware commit and tag pins -- label distinctly so a reviewer knows these change out-of-tree kernel-module source, not just a build tool version.

Main_MiSTer shared-library pins (libchdr commit, LZMA SDK tag) -- distinct label per the established per-pin-class convention, so a reviewer knows these change a userspace library ABI Main_MiSTer links against (liblzma-sdk's SONAME is the full version, so an SDK bump IS an ABI event by design), not kernel-module source or a build tool. NOTE (ADR 0023): matchDepNames cannot separate the two ip7z/7zip consumers, because package/lzma-sdk and package/7zip deliberately share that depName so one PR bumps both. So an ip7z/7zip PR carrying this label changes BOTH the liblzma-sdk ABI AND the 7zz archiver / the /media/fat/linux/7za updater binary -- review it as both.

Userspace controller-tooling pins. Its own label rather than driver-pin, per the established one-label-per-pin-class convention: driver-pin's reviewer contract is "this changes out-of-tree kernel-module source", and dualsensectl changes neither kernel-module source nor a library ABI Main_MiSTer links against (lib-pin's contract). It ships one self-contained CLI binary that nothing on the image invokes automatically, so the blast radius of a bad bump is an operator typing a command, not a boot or a link failure.

azcopy. Shares tool-pin's reviewer contract exactly -- one self-contained userspace CLI binary that nothing on the image invokes automatically, so a bad bump costs an operator a command, not a boot -- and so takes that label rather than a fourth one. It is a SEPARATE rule only so it can carry needs-manual-hash without editing dualsensectl's, which does not need it. needs-manual-hash is the same signal the RT kernel pin carried until 2026-08-17 and means precisely one thing: no automated step can refresh this package's .hash, so the bump PR is expected to arrive RED and stays red until a human runs package/azcopy/azcopy.hash's regeneration recipe. It is red-by-design, not a broken bot -- see that file and docs/azcopy.md section 5 for why a golang-package's hash cannot be curl'd.

SD-card payload pins (update_all.sh, wifi.sh, and the _Console cores snapshot fetched by scripts/fetch-sdcard-payload.sh). Label distinctly so a reviewer knows these change what a freshly-flashed sdcard.img installs, not a build tool or kernel-module source.
Keep CI container image digests (ubuntu:26.04@sha256:... in build.yml/release.yml/reproducibility.yml's `container:` blocks) pinned and updated in place.

GitHub Actions SHA-pinned `uses:` lines (with a trailing # vX.Y.Z comment) across build/release/reproducibility/publish-db workflows -- handled by Renovate's built-in github-actions manager (digest update, comment kept in sync). No custom manager needed; this rule just labels the PRs.
